class.name: JRPGReferenceScanner
class.brief_description: Finds every use of a JRPG database ID and reports references to missing or cleared entries.
class.description: Scans the [JRPGDatabase] tables, type lists and system data for ID references: traits, effects, learnings, drops, enemy actions, troop members and page conditions, actor classes and initial equipment, skill, weapon and armor types, elements, animations, the starting party, the start map, and the database-ID parameters of event commands ([method JRPGEventCommand.get_id_parameters]) in common events and troop pages. Map events live in map scenes: [method collect_map_references] and [method find_dangling_in_map] scan one map's data. Each reference is a [Dictionary] with [code]source[/code], [code]source_id[/code], [code]path[/code], [code]target[/code] and [code]target_id[/code]. [code]source[/code] and [code]target[/code] are table names (see [method JRPGDatabase.get_table_name]) or type lists ([code]elements[/code], [code]skill_types[/code], [code]weapon_types[/code], [code]armor_types[/code], [code]equip_types[/code]); [code]maps[/code] is the target of map IDs, which the project's [JRPGMapList] holds. System data references have the source [code]system[/code] and source ID 0. IDs 0 and below mean "none" and are never references. The database editor uses it to warn before clearing an entry or shrinking a table, and to list dangling references.

method.name: collect_map_references
method.description: Returns the references held by the commands of [param map]'s events (every page, child lists included): source [code]"maps"[/code], source_id the map's id, and a path such as [code]"event 3, page 1, commands[lb]2[rb].then_list[lb]0[rb].item_id"[/code]. A map's data lives in its scene: tools that load scenes pass it here.

method.name: collect_references
method.description: Returns every reference in [param database], in table order and then entry order, with the System data last.

method.name: describe
method.description: Returns where a reference is and what it points to, for reports, for example [code]Skill 4, effects[1].data_id: state 12[/code].

method.name: find_dangling
method.description: Returns the references whose target does not exist, with [code]problem[/code] set to [code]missing[/code] (beyond the table or type list, or a map that [param maps] does not list), or whose target was cleared, with [code]problem[/code] set to [code]blank[/code] (an entry or type without a name). Map references, such as the System's start map, are judged only when [param maps] is given.

method.name: find_dangling_in_map
method.description: Returns the references of [param map]'s events whose target does not exist or was cleared, judged as [method find_dangling] does.

method.name: find_uses
method.description: Returns the references to entry or type [param id] of [param target], for example before clearing it.

method.name: find_uses_from
method.description: Returns the references to [param first_id] and higher IDs of [param target], for example before shrinking a table to [code]first_id - 1[/code] entries.

method.name: get_id_target
method.description: Returns the table name (such as [code]"classes"[/code]) or type list (such as [code]"elements"[/code]) that the integer [param property] of [param object] points into when it holds one database ID, or an empty string when it is not such a reference. The editor uses this to show ID properties as lists of entries.

method.name: get_target_label
method.description: Returns the singular label of a table or type list for reports, such as [code]"Skill type"[/code] for [code]"skill_types"[/code]. Unknown names are returned unchanged.

method.name: get_target_names
method.description: Returns the names of the entries of a table, or the names of a type list, from [param database]. Index [code]i[/code] holds the name of ID [code]i + 1[/code]; an empty name is an empty entry. Returns an empty array for [code]"maps"[/code]: map IDs have gaps, and [JRPGMapList] holds the map names.
